description: This dataset contains groundwater-quality observations from sixty-four publicly accessible boreholes in central Tanzania. The research team samples twenty-two locations each in Dodoma and Singida and twenty in Tabora during three days in August 2020. GPS positions accompany pH, conductivity, hardness, major-ion, nitrate and fluoride measurements, collected along road routes totalling 1,344 kilometres. Mendeley version 2 provides two Excel workbooks free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is one short campaign, so the data do not resolve seasonal change or conditions at unsampled boreholes. Road-based selection and different field and laboratory measurement times are further limits on regional inference. A reviewer-assessed use is checking source-water suitability assumptions or mapping quality constraints in water-supply scenarios. platform-sei-weap-water-evaluation-and-adaptation-planning is a related allocation environment, but abstractions, aquifer yields and treatment parameters would require separate data. No workbook, interpolation or chemical-balance calculation was performed.
